# Run book: See the claims on your token

[Run books](README.md) | [User guide](../user-guide/see-who-you-are.md) | [Spec](../specs/see-who-you-are.md)

## Contents

- [Purpose](#purpose)

## Purpose

Inspect the claims the API sees on your token, the quickest way to debug roles and rights.

## Preconditions

- Sign-in is configured, or the API runs with identity disabled for local work.

## Verify

Automatically: `npx playwright test e2e/journeys.spec.ts -g "See the claims on your token"` (add `E2E_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8088` to run against the compose stack).

By hand, in the example web application at `/identity/me`:

1. **Open the current user screen.** The screen calls the API and lists every claim on the access token. Expect: The name claim is listed.

## Troubleshooting

**Table 1 — Known problems**

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 Unauthorized | Not signed in or the token expired | Sign in again |
| Expected role missing | The user does not have the role in the realm | Check the user in Keycloak and dev-users.md |

Related framework features: OoBDev.Identity; Keycloak (OIDC, JWT bearer).
